records.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is set with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then TTL is applied with a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This is not atomic; if the process crashes or errors between these calls, the key may be left without an expiry, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true forever for that `embed_url` (permanent throttling). records.issue_text: document.getElementById('discourse-comments') result is used without a null check, throwing a TypeError on pages that include embed.js without the div
records.rationale: In new app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` is followed by `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no null/undefined guard. If a page includes embed.js but does not have an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be null and `appendChild` will throw a TypeError at runtime.

records.issue_text: The loading page reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally, looping forever on permanent retrieval failure instead of showing an error
records.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds via `setTimeout`, and this template is rendered when no `topic_id` exists yet (`EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` then `render 'loading'`). If retrieval permanently fails (e.g., job/network/parsing issues), the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely with no error stat

records.issue_text: Adding force: true to an already-shipped migration is dangerous: re-running the migration drops and recreates the table, destroying data; existing migrations should not be edited
records.rationale: The diff edits an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it exists before creating it, so if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., rollback/redo in dev/test or in unusual recovery scenarios) it can destroy existing `top_topics` data.
